label: th:moments
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:moments}For every centered log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on ${\mathbb R}^n$
we have that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-moments-intro}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\exp\left(\frac{c}{n}\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast }(x)\right)\,d\mu(x)<\infty \end{equation}
where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, $\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}$ has finite moments of all orders.
head: environment

label: th:small-moments
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:small-moments}For every centered log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on ${\mathbb R}^n$
we have that
$$\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^2(\mu)}\leqslant cn\ln n$$
where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.
head: environment

label: th:rough
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:rough}There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that
$$\inf_{\mu }\Big(\inf\Big\{ {\mathbb E}_{\mu^N}\big[\mu (K_N)\big]: N\geqslant \exp (Cn\ln n)\Big\}\Big)\longrightarrow 1$$
as $n\to\infty $, where the first infimum is over all log-concave probability measures $\mu $ on ${\mathbb R}^n$.
head: environment

label: th:negative-phi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:negative-phi}There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that
$$J_{\mu}(p):=\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\frac{1}{\varphi_{\mu}^p(x)}\,d\mu (x)<\infty$$
for every log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and any $0<p\leqslant c/n$.
head: environment

label: th:T-measure
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:T-measure}For every log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\sup\{e^{\frac{1}{8}\frac{s}{n}}(1-\mu(T_s(\mu))):s>0\}\leqslant c_n,$$
where $c_n=\exp(n\ln n/8)$ is a constant depending only on $n$.
head: environment

label: prop:r-2
title: Proposition
body_md: \label{prop:r-2}For every $t\geqslant 5(n-1)$ we have that $\mu(R_t(\mu ))\geqslant 1-e^{-t/4}$.
head: environment

label: lem:r-1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\int_0^{\infty}r^{m}g(r)\,dr=1$. For $r>0$ we define
$$\varphi(r)=r^{m}g(r)\quad\hbox{and}\quad \Phi(r)=\int_0^r\varphi(u)\,du.$$
Note that $\varphi$ is a log-concave function with $\int_0^{\infty}\varphi(r)\,dr=1$.
Define $r_m$ as the unique solution of $(\ln g)^{\prime}(r)=-m/r$. Then, equivalently, we have
that $\varphi^{\prime}(r_m)=0$ and since $\varphi$ is log-concave and $\varphi(r_m)>0$ we conclude
that $\varphi(r_m)=\max(\varphi)$. From \eqref{eq:r-1} we know that
$$g(r)\geqslant e^{-m}g(0)$$
for all $0\leqslant r\leqslant r_m$. It follows that if $M:=g(r_m)$ then, for every $r>0$ that satisfies
$g(r)\geqslant e^{-(\alpha-1)m}M$ we have that $g(r)\geqslant e^{-\alpha m}g(0)$, and hence
$$\varrho_{\alpha m}\geqslant r^{\prime}:=\sup\{r>0:g(r)\geqslant e^{-(\alpha -1)m}M\}.$$
From the definition of $r^{\prime}$ it is clear that $r_m\leqslant r^{\prime}$.
Also, since $g(r^{\prime})=e^{-(\alpha-1)m}M$, from \eqref{eq:r-2} we see that $r^{\prime}\leqslant\alpha r_m$. It follows that
\begin{equation*}
\varphi(r^{\prime}) =\varphi(r_m)\left(\frac{r^{\prime}}{r_m}\right)^{m}\frac{g(r^{\prime})}{M}\leqslant
\varphi(r_m)\alpha^{m}e^{-(\alpha-1)m}\leqslant \varphi(r_m)e^{-\alpha m/4}=e^{-\alpha m/4}\max(\varphi).
\end{equation*}
The last inequality follows from the fact that $3\alpha \geqslant 4(\ln \alpha +1)$ when $\alpha\geqslant 5$.
It is not hard to check that $\psi(s)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(s))$ is concave on $(0,1)$.  Since $\varphi$
attains its maximum at $r_m$, we have that $\psi$ attains its maximum at $\Phi(r_m)$. Then, for any
$0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$, using the concavity of $\psi$ we can check that if
$s\geqslant \Phi(r_m)$ and $\psi(s)\leqslant\varepsilon\cdot\max(\psi)$
we must have that $s\geqslant 1-\varepsilon$. It follows that if $r\geqslant r_m$ and
$\varphi(r)\leqslant\varepsilon\cdot\max(\psi)=\varepsilon\cdot\max(\varphi)$ then
$\Phi(r)\geqslant 1-\varepsilon$. Since $r^{\prime}\geqslant r_m$ and $r^{\prime}$
satisfies $\varphi(r^{\prime})\leqslant e^{-\alpha m/4}\max(\varphi)$, we conclude that
$$\Phi(r^{\prime})\geqslant 1-e^{-\alpha m/4}.$$
The result follows from the fact that $\varrho_{\alpha m}\geqslant r^{\prime}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\xi\in S^{n-1}$ and consider the log-concave integrable function $g:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$
defined by $g(r)=f_{\mu}(r\xi)$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:r-1} with $m=n-1$ and $\alpha=t/m$ we see that
$$\int_0^{\varrho_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)}r^{n-1}f_{\mu}(r\xi)\,dr
\geqslant \left(1-e^{-t/4}\right)\int_0^{\infty}r^{n-1}f_{\mu}(r\xi)\,dr.$$
Then, integration in polar coordinates shows that
\begin{align*}\mu(R_t(\mu )) &=n\omega_n\int_{S^{n-1}}\int_0^{\varrho_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)}r^{n-1}f_{\mu}(r\xi)\,dr\,d\sigma(\xi)\\
&\geqslant \left(1-e^{-t/4}\right)\,n\omega_n\int_{S^{n-1}}\int_0^{\infty}r^{n-1}f_{\mu}(r\xi)\,dr\,d\sigma(\xi)=1-e^{-t/4},
\end{align*}
which is the assertion of the proposition.
head: environment
name: Proof of Proposition~$\ref{prop:r-2}$

label: rem:referee
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:referee}\rm The referee of this article has very kindly communicated to us the following very short and elegant proof
of Proposition~\ref{prop:r-2}. Consider the convex function $\psi$ defined by $e^{-\psi(x)}=f_{\mu}(x)/f_{\mu}(0)$. Note that $\psi(0)=0$.
Then
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{\psi(x)/2}d\mu(x) &=f_{\mu}(0)\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{-\psi(x)/2}dx=f_{\mu}(0)\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{-(\psi(x)+\psi(0))/2}dx\\
&\leqslant f_{\mu}(0)\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{-\psi(x/2)}dx=2^nf_{\mu}(0)\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{-\psi(x)}dx=2^n.
\end{align*}
For any $t>0$ we have $R_t(\mu)=\{x:\psi(x)\leqslant t\}$. From Markov's inequality we get
$$1-\mu(R_t(\mu))=\mu(\{x:\psi(x)>t\})\leqslant e^{-t/2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{\psi(x)/2}d\mu(x)\leqslant 2^ne^{-t/2}.$$
If $t\geqslant (4\ln 2)n$ then $2^ne^{-t/2}\leqslant e^{-t/4}$, and this implies that
$$\mu(R_t(\mu))\geqslant 1-e^{-t/4},\qquad\text{for all}\;t\geqslant (4\ln 2)n.$$
head: environment

label: prop:r-3
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:r-3}For every $s>t$ we have that
$$R_t(\mu )\subseteq e^{t/s}K_s(\mu ).$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi\in S^{n-1}$ and define $g:[0,\infty )\to [0,\infty )$ by
$g(r)=f_{\mu }(r\xi )$. By the definition of $K_s(\mu )$ we have
$$[\varrho_{K_s(\mu )}(\xi )]^s=\frac{s}{f_{\mu }(0)}\int_0^{\infty }r^{s-1}g(r)dr.$$
Since $g(r)\geqslant e^{-t}f_{\mu}(0)$ for all $0\leqslant r\leqslant\varrho_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)$ we see that
$$\int_0^{\infty }r^{s-1}g(r)dr\geqslant \int_0^{\varrho_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)}r^{s-1}g(r)dr
\geqslant e^{-t}f_{\mu}(0)\int_0^{\varrho_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)}r^{s-1}dr=\frac{f_{\mu}(0)}{s}e^{-t}[\varrho_{R_t(\mu )}(\xi )]^s.$$
It follows that $\varrho_{K_s(\mu )}(\xi )\geqslant e^{-t/s}\varrho_{R_t(\mu )}(\xi )$. Since $\xi\in S^{n-1}$
was arbitrary, this shows that $R_t(\mu )\subseteq e^{t/s}K_s(\mu )$.
head: environment

label: prop:r-4
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:r-4}Let $n\geqslant 3$. For every $t\geqslant 2n$ and any $\alpha\geqslant 5$ we have that
$$R_{\alpha t}(\mu )\supseteq \left(1-\frac{2n}{t}\right)K_t(\mu ).$$
Under the additional assumption that $\mu$ is even, we have that
$$R_{\alpha t}(\mu )\supseteq \left(1-e^{-\alpha t/5}\right)K_t(\mu ).$$
head: environment

label: eq:r-3
title: Proof
body_md:
Given any $\xi\in S^{n-1}$ consider the log-concave function $g:[0,\infty )\to [0,\infty )$ defined by
$g(r)=f_{\mu }(r\xi )$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:r-1} with $m=t-1$ we see that
$$\int_0^{\varrho_{R_{\alpha t}(\mu )}(\xi )}r^{t-1}g(r)dr\geqslant (1-e^{-\alpha t/5})\int_0^{\infty }r^{t-1}g(r)dr.$$
By the definition of $K_t(\mu )$ we have
$$\int_0^{\infty }r^{t-1}g(r)dr=\frac{f_{\mu }(0)}{t}[\varrho_{K_t(\mu )}(\xi )]^t.$$
On the other hand,
$$\int_0^{\varrho_{R_{\alpha t}(\mu )}(\xi )}r^{t-1}g(r)dr\leqslant \|f_{\mu}\|_{\infty }\int_0^{\varrho_{R_{\alpha t}(\mu )}(\xi )}r^{t-1}dr
=\frac{\|f_{\mu}\|_{\infty }}{t}[\varrho_{R_{\alpha t}(\mu )}(\xi )]^t.$$
Using also the fact that $\|f_{\mu}\|_{\infty }\leqslant e^nf_{\mu }(0)$ from \eqref{eq:frad-2}, we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:r-3}e^n[\varrho_{R_{\alpha (t-1)}(\mu )}(\xi )]^t
\geqslant (1-e^{-\alpha t/5})[\varrho_{K_t(\mu )}(\xi )]^t\end{equation}
and the result follows because
$$e^{-n/t}(1-e^{-\alpha t/5})^{1/t}\geqslant (1-n/t)(1-e^{-\alpha t/5})\geqslant
(1-n/t)^2\geqslant 1-2n/t.$$ When $\mu$ is even, the term $e^n$ does not appear
in \eqref{eq:r-3}, and thus we obtain an improved estimate.
head: environment

label: prop:1
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:1-1
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $v\in Z_t^+(\mu)$. We shall show that $\Lambda^{\ast }_{\mu }(v/c_s)\leqslant s$, where
$c_s\leqslant 1+\frac{2\ln s}{s}$. To this end, we should check that
\begin{equation*}\frac{1}{c_s}\langle u, v\rangle-\Lambda_\mu(u) \leqslant s\end{equation*}
for all $u\in{\mathbb R}^n$. For every $u\in{\mathbb R}^n$ we define $\beta_u$ by the equation
\begin{equation*}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\langle u, x\rangle_+^td\mu(x) = \beta_u^t.\end{equation*}
Then, $u/\beta_u\in M^+_t(\mu)$ and since $Z_t^+(\mu )=(M_t^+(\mu ))^{\circ }$
we have that $\langle u,v\rangle \leqslant \beta_u$. Note that, by H\"{o}lder's inequality, for all $s\geqslant t$ we have that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1-1}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\langle u, x\rangle_+^sd\mu(x)\geqslant \left(\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\langle u, x\rangle_+^td\mu(x)\right)^{s/t}=\beta_u^s.\end{equation}
For any $0<\delta<\beta_u$, using \eqref{eq:1-1} we see that
\begin{align*}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n} e^{\frac{\delta}{\beta_u}\langle u,x\rangle }d\mu(x) &\geqslant  \int_{{\mathbb R}^n} e^{\frac{\delta}{\beta_u}\langle
u,x\rangle}\mathds{1}_{\{x:\langle u,x\rangle \geqslant 0\}}(x)\,d\mu(x)
\geqslant \int_{{\mathbb R}^n} \frac{\delta^s\langle u, x\rangle_+^s}{s!\beta_u^s} \mathds{1}_{\{x:\langle
u,x\rangle \geqslant 0\}}(x)\,d\mu(x) \\
&=\int_{{\mathbb R}^n} \frac{\delta^s\langle u, x\rangle_+^s}{s!\beta_u^s}\,d\mu(x)
\geqslant\frac{\delta^s}{s!}.\end{align*}
So, $\Lambda_{\mu}(\delta u/\beta_u)\geqslant \ln\left(\frac{\delta^s}{s!}\right)$, and using the convexity of $\Lambda_{\mu}$
and the fact that $\Lambda_{\mu}(0)=0$ we obtain
\begin{equation*}\Lambda_{\mu}(u) \geqslant \frac{\beta_u}{\delta}\Lambda_{\mu}(\delta u/\beta_u)
\geqslant \beta_u\,\frac{1}{\delta}\ln\left(\frac{\delta^s}{s!}\right).\end{equation*} Therefore, for any $c>0$ we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1-3}\frac{1}{c}\langle u,v\rangle-\Lambda_{\mu}(u) \leqslant
\beta_u \left[\frac{1}{c}-\frac{1}{\delta}\ln\left(\frac{\delta^s}{s!}\right)\right].\end{equation}
The function $g_s(\delta)=\frac{1}{\delta}\ln\left(\frac{\delta^s}{s!}\right)$ attains its maximum value
at $\delta_s$ where $\delta_s$ satisfies $s=\ln\left(\frac{\delta^s}{s!}\right)$, i.e. $\delta_s=e(s!)^{1/s}$.
This maximum value is equal to $\max(g_s)=\frac{s}{\delta_s}=\frac{s}{e(s!)^{1/s}}$. So, if we choose $\delta=\delta_s$
and $c_s=\frac{1}{\max(g_s)}$, from \eqref{eq:1-3} we see that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1-4}\frac{1}{c_s}\langle u,v\rangle-\Lambda_{\mu}(u)\leqslant 0\end{equation}
for all $u\in\mathbb{R}^n$ that satisfy $\beta_u>\delta_s$. On the other hand, since $\mu$ is centered, we have that
$\Lambda_{\mu}(u)\geqslant 0$ for all $u\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and hence, for all $u\in\mathbb{R}^n$ that satisfy $\beta_u\leqslant\delta_s$ we have that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1-5}\frac{1}{c_s}\langle u,v\rangle -\Lambda_\mu(u) \leqslant \frac{1}{c_s}\beta_u\leqslant \frac{\delta_s}{c_s}=s.\end{equation}
This shows that
$$\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(v/c_s)=\sup\left\{\frac{1}{c_s}\langle u,v\rangle -\Lambda_{\mu}(u):u\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}
\leqslant s,$$
or equivalently $v\in c_sB_s$. We have thus proved that $Z_t^+\subseteq c_sB_s$ for all $s\geqslant t$ and it remains to
estimate the constant $c_s$. By Stirling's formula,
$$c_s=\frac{e}{s}\,(s!)^{1/s}\sim \frac{e}{s}\left(\frac{s}{e}\right)(2\pi s)^{\frac{1}{2s}}=(2\pi s)^{\frac{1}{2s}}\sim
1+\frac{\ln(2\pi s)}{2s}$$
as $s\to\infty$. It follows that if $s\geqslant t\geqslant t_0$ (where $t_0$ is a large enough constant) then $c_s\leqslant 1+\frac{2\ln s}{s}$.
head: environment

label: prop:B<Z
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:B<Z}Let $\mu $ be a centered log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
For any $t\geqslant 1$ and any $\delta\in (0,1)$ we have that
\begin{equation*}B_t(\mu) \subseteq (1+\delta)Z_{c_1t/\delta}^+(\mu)\end{equation*}
where $c_1>0$ is an absolute constant.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta\in (0,1)$ and $t\geqslant 1$. If $u\in M^+_s(\mu)$ then H\"{o}lder's inequality shows that
$\|\langle u,\cdot\rangle_+\|_k\leqslant \|\langle u,\cdot\rangle_+\|_s\leqslant 1$ for all $k\leqslant s$, and \eqref{eq:regularity}
implies that $\|\langle u,\cdot\rangle_+\|_k\leqslant \frac{ck}{s}\|\langle u,\cdot\rangle_+\|_s\leqslant \frac{ck}{s}$
for all $k>s$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Since $\frac{k}{(k!)^{1/k}}\to e$, we may choose an absolute constant $\gamma>0$ small enough so that $\frac{c\gamma k}{(k!)^{1/k}}\leqslant\frac{1}{2}$ for all $k\geqslant 1$.  It follows that
\begin{align*}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^n} e^{\langle \gamma su,x\rangle_+}d\mu(x)
&=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k!}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\langle \gamma su, x\rangle_+^kd\mu(x)
\leqslant \sum_{k\leqslant s}\frac{(\gamma s)^k}{k!}+\sum_{k>s}\frac{(\gamma s)^k}{k!}\left (\frac{ck}{s}\right )^k\\
&\leqslant e^{\gamma s}+\sum_{k>s}\frac{1}{2^k}\leqslant e^{\gamma s}+1\leqslant e^{\gamma s+1}\end{align*}
if $s\geqslant s_0$. Therefore, for any $u\in M^+_s(\mu)$ we get $\Lambda_{\mu}(\gamma su)\leqslant\gamma s+1$.

Now, let $v\notin (1+\delta)Z^+_s(\mu)$. We can find $u\in M^+_s(\mu)$ such that $\langle v,u\rangle> 1+\delta $ and then
\begin{equation*}\Lambda^{\ast }_{\mu }(v) \geqslant \langle v,\gamma su\rangle
-\Lambda_{\mu }(\gamma su)> (1+\delta)\gamma s -\gamma s-1=\delta\gamma s-1>t\end{equation*}
if we assume that $s\geqslant \frac{2t}{\gamma\delta}$. Therefore, $v\notin
B_t(\mu )$. This shows that $B_t(\mu)\subseteq (1+\delta)Z^+_{c_1t/\delta} (\mu)$, where $c_1=2/\gamma$.
head: environment

label: prop:floating-1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:floating-1}There exists $s_0\geqslant 1$ such that, for every centered log-concave
probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and any $s\geqslant s_0$,
$$T_s(\mu)\subseteq B_s(\mu)\subseteq T_{s+3\ln s}(\mu).$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We shall use a result of Brazitikos and Chasapis from \cite{Brazitikos-Chasapis-2024}: For every $x\in {\rm supp}(\mu)$
and any $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ we have that
$$\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)\geqslant (1-\varepsilon)\ln\left(\frac{1}{\varphi_{\mu}(x)}\right)
+\ln\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{2^{1-\varepsilon}}\right)=\ln\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{(2\varphi_{\mu}(x))^{1-\varepsilon}}\right).$$
Let $x\in B_s(\mu)$ and assume that $\varphi_{\mu}(x)<e^{-s-3\ln s}$. Then,
$$2\varphi_{\mu}(x)\leqslant e^{-s-3\ln s+\ln 2}<e^{-s-2\ln s}$$
provided that $s\geqslant 2$, and hence
$$s\geqslant \Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)\geqslant \ln\left(\varepsilon e^{(1-\varepsilon)(s+2\ln s)}\right)
=\ln\varepsilon +(1-\varepsilon)(s+2\ln s)$$
for every $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and any $s\geqslant 2$. The function $f(\varepsilon)=\ln\varepsilon +(1-\varepsilon)(s+2\ln s)$
attains its maximum at $\varepsilon =\frac{1}{s+2\ln s}$ and we must have
$$s\geqslant -\ln(s+2\ln s)+\left(1-\frac{1}{s+2\ln s}\right)(s+2\ln s)=s+2\ln s-\ln(s+2\ln s)-1.$$
It follows that $\ln(s+2\ln s)+1\geqslant 2\ln s$, which implies that $e(s+2\ln s)\geqslant s^2$, a contradiction if
$s\geqslant s_0$ for a large enough absolute constant $s_0>0$.

We have thus shown that if $s\geqslant s_0$ and $x\in B_s(\mu)$ then $\varphi_{\mu}(x)\geqslant e^{-s-3\ln s}$, i.e.
$B_s(\mu)\subseteq T_{s+3\ln s}(\mu)$. The inclusion $T_s(\mu)\subseteq B_s(\mu)$ is \eqref{eq:floating-1} above.
head: environment

label: lem:floating-2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:floating-2}Let $\mu$ be a centered log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
For any $\delta>0$ and any $t\geqslant 1$ we have that
$$T_{t\ln(1+\delta)}(\mu)\subseteq (1+\delta)Z_t^+(\mu).$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $x\notin (1+\delta)Z_t^+(\mu)$. Then, we may find $\delta^{\prime}>\delta$ and $\xi\in S^{n-1}$ such that
$x\in H=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,\xi\rangle \geqslant (1+\delta^{\prime})h_{Z_t^+}(\xi)\}$. From Markov's inequality we see
that
$$\mu(H)\leqslant (1+\delta^{\prime})^{-t} <(1+\delta)^{-t}=e^{-t\ln(1+\delta)},$$
therefore, $\varphi_{\mu}(x)\leqslant\mu(H)< e^{-t\ln(1+\delta)}$, which shows that $x\notin T_{t\ln(1+\delta)}(\mu)$.
The lemma follows.
head: environment

label: lem:2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:2}Let $\mu$ be a centered log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$. For
any $\delta>0$ and any Borel subset $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ we have that
$$\mu((1+\delta)A)\leqslant e^{2n\delta }\mu(A).$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that if $A\subset {\mathbb R}^n$ is a Borel set, then
$$\mu((1+\delta)A)=\int_{(1+\delta)A}f_{\mu}(x)\,dx=(1+\delta)^n\int_Af_{\mu}((1+\delta)x)\,dx.$$
Since $f_{\mu}$ is log-concave, we see that
$$f_{\mu}((1+\delta)x)\leqslant f_{\mu}(x)\left(\frac{f_{\mu}(x)}{f_{\mu}(0)}\right)^{\delta}\leqslant e^{n\delta}f_{\mu}(x)$$
for every $x\in {\mathbb R}^n$, because $f_{\mu}(x)\leqslant e^nf_{\mu}(0)$ by \eqref{eq:frad-2}. It follows that
\begin{equation*}\mu((1+\delta)A)\leqslant (1+\delta)^ne^{n\delta}\mu(A)\leqslant e^{2n\delta}\mu(A)\end{equation*}
as claimed.
head: environment

label: prop:3-weak
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:3-weak}Let $\mu $ be an isotropic log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$. For any $\delta\in (0,1)$
and any $t\geqslant C_{\delta }n\ln n$ we have that $$\mu ((1+\delta )Z_t^+(\mu ))\geqslant 1-e^{-c\delta t}$$
where $C_{\delta }=C\delta^{-1}\ln\left(2/\delta\right)$ and $C,c>0$ are absolute positive constants.
head: environment

label: th:moments-weak
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:moments-weak}Let $\mu$ be a centered log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$.
For every $0<p<1$ we have that
$$\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast }(x)|^p\,d\mu(x)<\infty .$$
head: environment

label: eq:moments-1
title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\mu$ is isotropic. Let $0<p<q<1$. Let $t>1$ that will be chosen appropriately large
and apply Proposition~\ref{prop:3-weak} with $\delta =\frac{\ln t}{ct^q}$. Then, we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:moments-1}\mu \left(\left(1+\frac{\ln t}{ct^q}\right)Z_t^+(\mu )\right)\geqslant 1-e^{-t^{1-q}\ln t}\end{equation}
provided that $t\geqslant C_1(q)t^qn\ln n$, or equivalently $t\geqslant t_n=C_2(q)(n\ln n)^{\frac{1}{1-q}}$.
Now, let $t\geqslant t_n$. From Proposition~\ref{prop:1} we see that
$$ \left(1+\frac{\ln t}{ct^q}\right)Z_t^+(\mu )\subseteq \left(1+\frac{\ln t}{ct^q}\right)
\left(1+\frac{\ln t}{t}\right)B_t(\mu)$$
and applying Lemma~\ref{lem:2} twice we obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:moments-2}\mu \left(\left(1+\frac{\ln t}{ct^q}\right)Z_t^+(\mu )\right)
&\leqslant \exp\left(\frac{2n\ln t}{ct^q}+\frac{2n\ln t}{t}\right)\mu(B_t(\mu))\leqslant \exp\left(\frac{4n\ln t}{ct^q}\right)\mu(B_t(\mu))\\
\nonumber &\leqslant \left(1-\frac{4n\ln t}{ct^q}\right)^{-1}\mu(B_t(\mu)).\end{align}
From \eqref{eq:moments-1} and \eqref{eq:moments-2} we get
$$\mu(B_t(\mu))\geqslant \left(1-e^{-t^{1-q}\ln t}\right)\left(1-\frac{4n\ln t}{ct^q}\right)\geqslant
1-\frac{8n\ln t}{ct^q}$$
if $t\geqslant s_n$ where $s_n\geqslant t_n$ is large enough and depends only on $n$ (note that
$\exp(t^{1-q}\ln t)\geqslant ct^q/(4n\ln t)$ for large enough $t$, independently from $n$).
Now, we write
\begin{align*}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)|^pd\mu(x)
&=\int_0^{\infty}pt^{p-1}\mu(\{x:\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)>t\})\,dt =\int_0^{\infty}pt^{p-1}(1-\mu(B_t(\mu)))\,dt\\
&=\int_0^{s_n}pt^{p-1}(1-\mu(B_t(\mu)))\,dt+\int_{s_n}^{\infty}pt^{p-1}(1-\mu(B_t(\mu)))\,dt\\
&\leqslant \int_0^{s_n}pt^{p-1}\,dt+\frac{8np}{c}\int_{s_n}^{\infty}t^{p-1}\frac{\ln t}{t^q}\,dt\\
&=s_n^p+\frac{8np}{c}\int_{s_n}^{\infty}\frac{\ln t}{t^{1+q-p}}dt<+\infty\end{align*}
where the last integral converges because $1+q-p>1$.
head: environment

label: lem:gamma-ball
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gamma-ball}Let $\mu$ be an isotropic log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$.
For any $t\geqslant 20n$ we have that
$$R_t(\mu)\supseteq  \frac{1}{3}B_2^n.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $r:=r(R_t(\mu))$ denote the inradius of $R_t(\mu)$ with respect to the origin. Then there exists $\xi\in S^{n-1}$ such that
$h_{R_t(\mu)}(\xi)\leqslant r$, and consequently
$$R_t(\mu)\subseteq \{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,\xi\rangle \leqslant r\}.$$
We decompose this half-space as
$$\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,\xi\rangle \leqslant r\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,\xi\rangle \leqslant 0\}\cup \{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:0<\langle x,\xi\rangle \leqslant r\}.$$
Since $\mu$ is centered, Gr\"{u}nbaum's lemma (see~\cite[Lemma~2.2.6]{BGVV-book}) yields 
$$\mu(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,\xi\rangle\leqslant 0\})\leqslant 1-\frac{1}{e}.$$
Let $F_{\xi}=\{t\xi:t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ be the one-dimensional subspace spanned by $\xi$.
Since $\mu$ is isotropic, the one-dimensional marginal $$g_{\xi}(t)=(\pi_{F_{\xi}}(f))(t)=\int_{F_{\xi}^{\perp}}f(y+t\xi )\,dy$$
is an isotropic log-concave density on $\mathbb{R}$ (see~\cite[Proposition~5.1.11]{BGVV-book}). Consequently,
\begin{equation*}\|g_{\xi}\|_{\infty}=L_{g_{\xi}}\leqslant 1.\end{equation*}
Therefore,
$$\mu(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:0<\langle x,\xi\rangle\leqslant r\})=\int_0^r\left(\int_{F_{\xi}^{\perp}}f(y+t\xi)\,dy\right)\,dt=\int_0^rg_{\xi}(t)\,dt\leqslant r.$$
Combining these estimates and using Proposition~\ref{prop:r-2}, we obtain
$$1-e^{-t/4}\leqslant \mu(R_t(\mu))\leqslant 1-\frac{1}{e}+r.$$
This implies 
$$r\geqslant e^{-1}-e^{-t/5}\geqslant e^{-1}-e^{-4}\geqslant 1/3,$$
as claimed.
head: environment

label: lem:level-B
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:level-B}Let $\mu$ be an isotropic log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$. For
any $\delta\in (0,1)$ and $t\geqslant n\ln n$ we have that
$$(1-\delta)R_t(\mu)\subseteq T_{g(t,\delta)}$$
where $g(t,\delta)\leqslant 2t+n\ln(1/\delta)$. In particular, if $\delta =e^{-t/2}$ we get
$$(1-e^{-t/2})R_t(\mu)\subseteq T_{nt}(\mu).$$
Note that the same inclusions hold with $T_{g(t,\delta)}$ replaced by $B_{g(t,\delta)}$, by~\eqref{eq:floating-1}.
head: environment

label: eq:delta
title: Proof
body_md:
From Lemma~\ref{lem:gamma-ball} we know that $R_t(\mu)\supseteq \frac{1}{3}B_2^n$. Let $x\in (1-\delta)R_t(\mu)$.
Since $(\delta/3)B_2^n\subseteq \delta R_t(\mu)$ we have that
$$B(x,\delta/3):=x+(\delta/3)B_2^n\subseteq (1-\delta)R_t(\mu)+\delta R_t(\mu)=R_t(\mu).$$
Then, if $H$ is a closed half-space such that $x\in\partial(H)$ we have that $H\cap B(x,\delta/3)\subseteq R_t(\mu)$,
and hence $f_{\mu}(y)\geqslant e^{-t}f_{\mu}(0)$ for all $y\in H\cap B(x,\delta/3)$. Since $H\cap B(x,\delta/3)$
is half of a ball of radius $\delta/3$, it follows that
$$\mu(H)\geqslant \int_{H\cap B(x,\delta/3)}f_{\mu}(y)\,d\mu(y)\geqslant e^{-t}f_{\mu}(0)\,|H\cap B(x,\delta/3)|
=e^{-t}f_{\mu}(0)\,\frac{\omega_n}{2}(\delta/3)^n.$$
Now, recall that $f_{\mu}(0)\geqslant e^{-n}\|f_{\mu}\|_{\infty}=e^{-n}L_{\mu}^n\geqslant (c_1/e)^n$ because $L_{\mu}\geqslant c_1$
for some absolute constant $c_1>0$, and $\frac{\omega_n}{2}\geqslant \left(\frac{c_2}{n}\right)^{n/2}$ for some absolute
constant $c_2>0$. Since $H$ was arbitrary, by the definition of $\varphi_{\mu}$ we get
$$\varphi_{\mu}(x)\geqslant e^{-t}\left(\frac{c_3}{n}\right)^{n/2}\delta^n=e^{-g(t,\delta)},$$
with $c_3=c_1^2c_2/(9e^2)$, where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:delta}g(t,\delta)=t+\frac{n}{2}\ln(c_4n)+n\ln(1/\delta)\end{equation}
with $c_4=1/c_3$. Since $t\geqslant n\ln n$, we see that $\frac{n}{2}\ln(c_4n)\leqslant t$ and the first assertion of the lemma follows.
For the second assertion, note that $g(t,e^{-t/2})\leqslant 2t+\frac{n}{2}t=\frac{n+4}{2}t\leqslant nt$ if $n\geqslant 4$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As we observed in the beginning of this section,
we may assume that $\mu$ is isotropic. Let $t_n:=n\ln n$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:level-B} and Proposition~\ref{prop:floating-1} we know that
if $t\geqslant t_n$ then
$$R_t(\mu)\subseteq (1+2e^{-t/2})T_{nt}(\mu)\subseteq (1+2e^{-t/2})B_{nt}(\mu).$$
Moreover, Proposition~\ref{prop:r-2} shows that $\mu(R_t(\mu ))\geqslant 1-e^{-t/4}$. Combining these facts
with Lemma~\ref{lem:2} we get
$$1-e^{-t/4}\leqslant \mu(R_t(\mu)) \leqslant \exp\left(4n\,e^{-t/2}\right)\mu(B_{nt}(\mu))\leqslant (1+8ne^{-t/2})\mu(B_{nt}(\mu)),$$
which finally gives
$$\mu(B_{nt}(\mu))\geqslant 1-e^{-t/8}$$
if $n\geqslant n_0$ for some fixed $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$. Now, we write
\begin{align*}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\exp\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)/(16n)\right)d\mu(x)
&=1+\frac{1}{16}\int_0^{\infty}e^{\frac{t}{16}}\mu(\{x\in {\mathbb R}^n:\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)>nt\})\,dt\\
&\leqslant 1+\frac{1}{16}\int_0^{t_n}e^{\frac{t}{16}}\,dt
+\frac{1}{16}\int_{t_n}^{\infty}e^{\frac{t}{16}}(1-\mu(B_{nt}(\mu)))\,dt\\
&\leqslant e^{\frac{t_n}{16}}+\frac{1}{16}\int_{t_n}^{\infty}e^{\frac{t}{16}}e^{-\frac{t}{8}}dt
=e^{\frac{t_n}{16}}+\frac{1}{16}\int_{t_n}^{\infty}e^{-\frac{t}{16}}dt \leqslant 2e^{\frac{t_n}{16}}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we have the assertion of the theorem with $c=\frac{1}{16}$.
head: environment
name: Proof of Theorem~$\ref{th:moments}$

title: Remark
body_md:
\rm We can obtain an upper bound on the Orlicz norm
$$\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^{\psi_1}(\mu)}:=\inf\left\{r>0: \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\exp\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)/r\right)d\mu(x)\leqslant 2\right\}$$
corresponding to $\psi_1(t)=e^t-1$, using H\"{o}lder's inequality. We write
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\exp\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)/r\right)d\mu(x)\leqslant \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\exp\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)/(16n)\right)d\mu(x)\right)^{\frac{16n}{r}}
\leqslant 2^{\frac{16n}{r}}e^{\frac{nt_n}{r}}$$
for any $r>16n$, and then choosing $r_0=\frac{32}{\ln 2}nt_n$ we check that $\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^{\psi_1}(\mu)}\leqslant r_0\approx n^2\ln n$.
head: environment

label: th:small-moments-p
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:small-moments-p}For every centered log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on ${\mathbb R}^n$
and any $1\leqslant p\leqslant c_1n$ we have that
$$\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^p(\mu)}\leqslant c_2pn\ln n$$
where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute constants.
head: environment

label: eq:for-theorem-4.2-1
title: Proof
body_md:
As in the previous proof, we may assume that $\mu$ is isotropic.
Let $t_n:=n\ln n$. Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:floating-1} and Lemma~\ref{lem:level-B} with
$\delta=t^{-p-2}$, or more precisely using \eqref{eq:delta}, we see that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:for-theorem-4.2-1}(1-t^{-p-2})R_t(\mu)\subseteq T_{g(t,t^{-p-2})}(\mu)\subseteq B_{g(t,t^{-p-2})}(\mu)\end{equation}
where 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:for-theorem-4.2-2}g(t,t^{-(p+2)})=t+\frac{n}{2}\ln(c_4n)+(p+2)n\ln t\leqslant 2(p+3)t\end{equation}
because the function $m(t)=\frac{t}{\ln t}$ is increasing on $[e,\infty)$ and hence
$\frac{n}{2}\leqslant \frac{n\ln n}{\ln(n\ln n)} \leqslant \frac{t}{\ln t}$ for all $t\geqslant t_n$, which
implies that $n\ln t\leqslant 2t$ for all $t\geqslant t_n$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:2} it follows that
$$\mu(B_{2(p+3)t})(\mu)\geqslant e^{-4n/t^{p+2}}\mu(R_t(\mu))\geqslant  e^{-4n/t^{p+2}}(1-e^{-t/4})\geqslant 1-\frac{8n}{t^{p+2}}>1-\frac{1}{t^{p+1}}$$
for all $t\geqslant t_n$ and all $0<p\leqslant n/8$ (here we use the fact that $\frac{t}{4}>(p+2)\ln t$ if $t\geqslant t_n$ and $p\leqslant n/8$,
which implies that $e^{-t/4}<2n/t^{p+2}$). Then, we write
\begin{align*}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)/2(p+3)|^pd\mu(x)
&=\int_0^{\infty}pt^{p-1}\mu(\{x\in {\mathbb R}^n:\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)>2(p+3)t\})\,dt\\
&=\int_0^{\infty}pt^{p-1}(1-\mu(B_{2(p+3)t}(\mu)))\,dt\\
&\leqslant t_n^p+\int_{t_n}^{\infty}pt^{p-1}\,\frac{1}{t^{p+1}}\,dt
\leqslant t_n^p+\frac{p}{t_n}.
\end{align*}
It follows that $\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^p(\mu)}\leqslant cpt_n=cpn\ln n$, for some absolute constant $c>0$.
head: environment

label: rem:optimal
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:optimal}\rm The upper bound of Theorem~\ref{th:small-moments} is sharp: a computation in
\cite{BGP-threshold} shows that
$$\|\Lambda_{\mu_{D_n}}^{\ast}\|_1\approx \|\Lambda_{\mu_{D_n}}^{\ast}\|_2\approx n\ln n$$
where $D_n$ is the centered Euclidean ball of volume $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu_{D_n}$ is the
uniform measure on $D_n$. On the other hand, it was proved in \cite{BGP-depth} that if $\mu$ is a log-concave
probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$, $n\geqslant n_0$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}e^{-\Lambda_{\mu }^{\ast}(x)}\,d\mu(x) \leqslant \exp\left(-cn/L_{\mu }^2\right).$$
From Jensen's inequality we immediately get
$$\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_1=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\Lambda_{\mu }^{\ast}(x)\,d\mu(x) \geqslant cn/L_{\mu }^2\geqslant c_1n.$$
This lower bound is also optimal, as one can check from the example of the uniform measure on the cube $C_n=\left[-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}\right]^n$. Summarizing, for any centered log-concave probability measure
$\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ we have that
$$c_1n\leqslant \|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^1(\mu)}\leqslant\|\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}\|_{L^2(\mu)}\leqslant c_2n\ln n,$$
where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute constants.
head: environment

label: prop:3
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:3}Let $\mu $ be a centered log-concave probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$.
For any $\delta\in \left(\frac{3}{n},1\right)$
and any $t\geqslant \frac{c_1}{\delta}n\ln n$ we have that
$$\mu ((1+\delta )Z_t^+(\mu ))\geqslant 1-e^{-c_2\delta t}$$
where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute positive constants.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:B<Z} shows that for any $m\geqslant 1$ and any $\eta\in (0,1)$ we have that
\begin{equation*}B_m(\mu) \subseteq (1+\eta)Z_{cm/\eta}^+(\mu)\end{equation*}
where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Now, from Lemma~\ref{lem:level-B} and Proposition~\ref{prop:floating-1} we know that if $s\geqslant n\ln n$ then
$$(1-\eta)R_s(\mu)\subseteq B_{g(s,\eta)}$$
where $g(s,\eta)\leqslant 2s+n\ln(1/\eta)$. Assuming that $\frac{1}{n}<\eta<\frac{1}{3}$ we see that
$g(s,\eta)\leqslant 3s$ and hence
$$R_s(\mu)\subseteq\frac{1}{1-\eta}B_{3s}\subseteq \frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}Z_{3cs/\eta}^+(\mu)
\subseteq (1+3\eta)Z_{3cs/\eta}^+(\mu)$$
for every $s\geqslant n\ln n$, because $\eta<\frac{1}{3}$ implies that $\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}\leqslant 1+3\eta$.
Since $s\geqslant 5n$, we may also apply Proposition~\ref{prop:r-2} to get $\mu(R_s(\mu ))\geqslant 1-e^{-s/4}$.
It follows that
$$\mu((1+3\eta)Z_{3cs/\eta}^+(\mu))\geqslant 1-e^{-s/4}$$
for every $s\geqslant n\ln n$ and any $\eta\in (1/n,1/3)$. Setting $\delta=3\eta$ and $t=3cs/\eta=9cs/\delta$
we get the assertion of the proposition.

label: th:non-sharp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:non-sharp}There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that
$$\inf_{\mu }\Big(\inf\Big\{ {\mathbb E}_{\mu^N}\big[\mu (K_N)\big]: N\geqslant \exp (Cn\ln n)\Big\}\Big)\longrightarrow 1$$
as $n\to\infty $, where the first infimum is over all log-concave probability measures $\mu $ on ${\mathbb R}^n$.
head: environment

label: eq:conditionC1
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Since the expectation
${\mathbb E}_{\mu^N}\big[\mu (K_N)\big]$ is a affinely invariant quantity, we may assume that $\mu$ is isotropic.
Let $t_n:=n\ln n$. In the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:small-moments} (see \eqref{eq:for-theorem-4.2-1} and \eqref{eq:for-theorem-4.2-2}) we saw that
$$\mu(T_{10t}(\mu))>1-1/t^3$$
for all $t\geqslant t_n$. By the definition of the family $\{T_t(\mu)\}_{t>0}$, for any $x\in T_{10t}(\mu)$ we have
\begin{equation*}\varphi_{\mu }(x)\geqslant e^{-10t}.\end{equation*}
We use the following standard lemma (which is stated in this form in \cite[Lemma~3]{Chakraborti-Tkocz-Vritsiou-2021};
for a proof see \cite{DFM} or \cite[Lemma~4.1]{Gatzouras-Giannopoulos-2009}): For every Borel subset $A$ of ${\mathbb R}^n$ we have that
$$1-\mu^N(K_N\supseteq A)\leqslant 2\binom{N}{n}\left (1-\inf_{x\in A}\varphi_{\mu }(x)\right)^{N-n}.$$
Therefore,
$${\mathbb E}_{\mu^N}[\mu (K_N)]\geqslant \mu (A)\left (1-2\binom{N}{n}\left (1-\inf_{x\in A}\varphi_{\mu }(x)\right)^{N-n}\right).$$
Setting $A=T_{10t}(\mu)$ we get
\begin{align*}\mu^N\Big(K_N\supseteq T_{10t}(\mu)\Big)
&\geqslant 1-2\binom{N}{n}\left [1-e^{-10t}\right]^{N-n}\\
&\geqslant 1-\left(\frac{2eN}{n}\right)^n\exp \left(-(N-n)e^{-10t}\right).
\end{align*}
This last quantity tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty $ if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conditionC1}n\ln (4eN/n)<(N-n)e^{-10t},\end{equation}
and we easily check that \eqref{eq:conditionC1} holds true if $t\geqslant t_n$ and $N\geqslant \exp (Ct)$ for a large enough absolute constant $C>0$. 
Therefore, if $N\geqslant \exp (Cn\ln n)$ we see that
\begin{align*}{\mathbb E}_{\mu^N}\left[\mu (K_N)\right]
&\geqslant \mu (T_{10t_n}(\mu))\times \mu^N\Big(K_N\supseteq T_{10t_n}(\mu)\Big)\\
&\geqslant \big(1-t_n^{-3}\big)\left[1-\left(\frac{2eN}{n}\right)^n\exp \left(-(N-n)e^{-10t_n}\right)\right]\longrightarrow 1
\end{align*}
as $n\to\infty $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\mu$ is centered.
The theorem follows immediately if we combine Theorem~\ref{th:moments}
with the inequality
$$\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)\geqslant \ln\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{(2\varphi_{\mu}(x))^{1-\varepsilon}}\right).$$
for every $x\in {\rm supp}(\mu)$ and any $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ (this is a result of Brazitikos and Chasapis from \cite{Brazitikos-Chasapis-2024} that we have already used in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:floating-1}).
Choosing $\varepsilon=1/2$ we get
$$\frac{1}{2^{3/2}\varphi_{\mu}(x)^{1/2}}\leqslant e^{\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)}$$
and hence
$$J_{\mu}(p):=\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\frac{1}{\varphi_{\mu}^p(x)}\,d\mu (x)\leqslant
2^{3p}{\mathbb E}\,\big[e^{2p\Lambda_{\mu}^{\ast}(x)}\big]<\infty$$
if $2p\leqslant c/n$ where $c>0$ is the absolute constant from Theorem~\ref{th:moments}.

name: Proof of Theorem~$\ref{th:negative-phi}$

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
We may also assume that $\mu$ is centered. In the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:moments} we saw that if $t\geqslant n\ln n$ then
$R_t(\mu)\subseteq (1+2e^{-t/2})T_{nt}(\mu)$, which implies that $\mu(T_{nt}(\mu))\geqslant 1-e^{-t/8}$. Equivalently, if $s\geqslant n^2\ln n$ then
$$\mu(T_s(\mu))\geqslant  1-e^{-s/(8n)},$$
which shows that $e^{s/(8n)}(1-\mu(T_s(\mu)))\leqslant 1$. It follows that
$$\sup\{e^{s/(8n)}(1-\mu(T_s(\mu))):s>0\}\leqslant \exp(n^2\ln n/(8n))$$
and the theorem follows with $c=1/8$ and $c_n=\exp(n\ln n/8)$.
